title: Sorting the restock list before you spend
target: How the restock screens in TCG Card Shop Simulator are arranged: a screen for browsing and a screen for adding to the cart, sort controls and page buttons, a running total for the cart, and a notification of what went into it.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A minute to use the screens

steps.do: Open the restock list rather than buying blind, because browsing and adding to the cart are separate screens.
steps.because: adding to the cart and browsing it are separate screens (RestockItemScreen, RestockItemAddToCartScreen)

steps.do: Sort before you shop, because the list has a sort screen and a set of sort buttons of its own.
steps.because: the list has a sort screen and sort buttons (m_SortUIScreen, m_SortBtnList)

steps.do: Move through the list in pages, because each page has a highlighted button that shows where you are.
steps.because: the panel list has page buttons that highlight (m_RestockItemPanelUIList, m_PageButtonHighlightList)

steps.do: Watch the running total rather than adding prices up in your head.
steps.because: the screen carries a total cost text (m_TotalCostText)

steps.do: Check how many lines are in the cart before paying, because the count has a readout of its own.
steps.because: the screen carries a total cart item count text (m_TotalCartItemCountText)

steps.do: Take the cart to its checkout screen when it is right, because the cart is paid for on a screen of its own.
steps.because: the cart is paid for on a checkout screen of its own (m_RestockItemCheckoutScreen)

steps.do: Use the tabletop screen for games rather than the card list, because tabletop games restock through a screen of their own.
steps.because: tabletop games restock through a screen of their own (RestockItemBoardGameScreen)

steps.do: Keep an eye on the cart notification, because adding something tells you it went in rather than leaving you to count rows.
steps.because: the screen carries a cart notification (m_CartNotification)

commonMistakes: Buying from the browsing screen and never opening the cart.
Working down an unsorted list and filling the cart with the wrong things.
Adding a line and not noticing the cart notification.
Paying without checking the total cost readout.
Going to the card list for tabletop games, which have a screen of their own.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Identifiers are listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
